messages.author: 51f6394a841f1b3c
messages.subject: Daytime naps
parts:
Hi Vincent, 

As you know I am analyzing the sleep data of 2 groups of children currently aged 3 years, wearing a wrist actiwatch. 
I just saw in the vignette 2.3.3.2 Advanced sleep log that I can add columns relating to napping time and nonwear time and that this is used for napping analysis. 

However, if I take a look at the big PDF file I see that  you wrote by argument  g.part5.classifyNaps:  "the only option is "hip3yr", which corresponds to a model trained with hip data in 3-3.5 olds trained with parent diary data". 
So I think this is not usable for my wrist worn data? 

For  the estimation of the 24-h sleep duration (so including daytime naps) I now use the nocturnal sleep duration + the " accumulated sustained inactivity bouts during the day" for at least 15 minutes as we discussed before. 

I hope you can clarify my question. Thanks a lot again! 
Best, Alja

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Daytime naps
parts:
Hi Alja,

The 'nap' detection work is only an explorative functionality trained for hip data in 3-3.5 year olds. Ideally more methodological research is needed to tailor this to other wear locations and age groups.

The idea has been to first facilitate that users can include nap and non-wear in sleeplogs,  which is now working. Next step would be to use this in studies for training nap-detection algorithms. So, depending on the sample size of your study it may be possible to train a separate model for wrist data. 

Best wishes,
Vincent
